title: Too good for it, i
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
logline: A second envelope from Portland. This one is opened, on the page. Wood is magnificent about it.

panels.composition: Wood's table. A new envelope, PNCA, opened. The letter out. WOOD reading it standing up. BARNABY.

balloons.text: '...pleased to offer...' Of course they are.

image.prompt: a young man standing at his bedroom table reading a letter from an opened envelope, a dog looking up, a crowded corkboard behind, brush-pen black and white

panels.composition: The letter: a partial scholarship. The number is drawn as a smudge. Wood's thumb near it.
props: the letter with a smudged number

image.prompt: close-up of a typed acceptance letter with one figure smudged into illegibility, a thumb nearby
image.notes: The amount is never legible. 'Modest,' per the brief.

balloons.text: A commercial racket designed to castrate raw vision. Four years of being told what a line is by people who've never cut mat board.

image.prompt: a young man with his arms spread wide holding a letter and orating to an unimpressed dog under a table

panels.composition: The letter on the corkboard, pinned over the bus schedule. Wood already back at the strip. The dog asleep. The letter looking very much like a thing that has been kept.
props: letter pinned over the bus schedule

image.prompt: an acceptance letter pinned to a corkboard on top of a bus schedule, a young man drawing at the table below, a dog asleep, no words
image.notes: The strip says he's above it. The strip pins it up.

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: The delusion-and-leak pattern: the speech and the thumbtack in the same strip.
